{{Orphan|date=August 2023}}

In [[geometric graph theory]], and the theory of [[structural rigidity]], a '''parallel redrawing''' of a [[graph drawing]] with straight edges in the [[Euclidean plane]] or higher-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] is another drawing of the same graph such that all edges of the second drawing are parallel to their corresponding edges in the first drawing. A '''parallel morph''' of a graph is a continuous family of drawings, all parallel redrawings of each other.

Parallel redrawings include [[Translation (geometry)|translations]], [[Scaling (geometry)|scaling]], and other modifications of the drawing that change it more locally. For instance, for graphs drawn as the vertices or edges of a [[simple polyhedron]], a parallel drawing can be obtained by translating the plane of one of the polyhedron's face, and adjusting the positions of the vertices and edges that border that face.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Bolker | first1 = Ethan
 | last2 = Guillemin | first2 = Victor
 | last3 = Holm | first3 = Tara
 | arxiv = math/0206103
 | title = How is a graph like a manifold?
 | year = 2002| bibcode = 2002math......6103B}}.</ref> A polyhedron is said to be '''tight''' if its only parallel redrawings are similarities (combinations of translation and scaling); among the [[Platonic solid]]s, the [[cube]] and [[dodecahedron]] are not tight (because of the possibility of translating one face while keeping the others fixed), but the [[tetrahedron]], [[octahedron]], and [[icosahedron]] are tight.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Ward | first = Thomas
 | arxiv = math/0503569
 | contribution = Mixing and tight polyhedra
 | doi = 10.1214/074921706000000194
 | mr = 2306198
 | pages = 169–175
 | publisher = Inst. Math. Statist., Beachwood, OH
 | series = IMS Lecture Notes Monogr. Ser.
 | title = Dynamics & stochastics
 | volume = 48
 | year = 2006| isbn = 0-940600-64-1
 | s2cid = 16378875
 }}.</ref>

In three dimensions, even for drawings where all edges are axis-parallel and the drawing forms the boundary of a [[polyhedron]], there may exist parallel redrawings that cannot be connected by a parallel morph.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Biedl | first1 = Therese | author1-link = Therese Biedl
 | last2 = Lubiw | first2 = Anna | author2-link = Anna Lubiw
 | last3 = Spriggs | first3 = Michael J.
 | doi = 10.1016/j.comgeo.2008.09.006
 | issue = 5
 | journal = [[Computational Geometry (journal)|Computational Geometry]]
 | mr = 2512668
 | pages = 395–402
 | title = Morphing polyhedra with parallel faces: counterexamples
 | volume = 42
 | year = 2009| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> For two-dimensional planar drawings, with parallel edges required to preserve their orientation, a morph always exists when the [[slope number]] is two, but it is [[NP-hard]] to determine the existence of a morph for three or more slopes.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Biedl | first1 = Therese | author1-link = Therese Biedl
 | last2 = Lubiw | first2 = Anna | author2-link = Anna Lubiw
 | last3 = Spriggs | first3 = Michael J.
 | contribution = Morphing planar graphs while preserving edge directions
 | doi = 10.1007/11618058_2
 | mr = 2244496
 | pages = 13–24
 | publisher = Springer | location = Berlin
 | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
 | title = Graph Drawing: 13th International Symposium, GD 2005, Limerick, Ireland, September 12-14, 2005, Revised Papers
 | volume = 3843
 | year = 2006| doi-access = free
 | isbn = 978-3-540-31425-7 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Biedl | first1 = Therese | author1-link = Therese Biedl
 | last2 = Lubiw | first2 = Anna | author2-link = Anna Lubiw
 | last3 = Petrick | first3 = Mark
 | last4 = Spriggs | first4 = Michael
 | doi = 10.1145/2500118
 | issue = 4
 | journal = ACM Transactions on Algorithms
 | mr = 3119787
 | page = Art. 29, 24
 | title = Morphing orthogonal planar graph drawings
 | volume = 9
 | year = 2013| s2cid = 122564585 }}.</ref>
Any parallel morph can be parameterized so that the each point moves with constant speed along a line. The graphs that remain planar throughout such a motion can be derived from [[Pseudotriangle|pseudotriangulations]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Streinu | first = Ileana | authorlink = Ileana Streinu
 | contribution = Parallel-redrawing mechanisms, pseudo-triangulations and kinetic planar graphs
 | doi = 10.1007/11618058_38
 | mr = 2244531
 | pages = 421–433
 | publisher = Springer | location = Berlin
 | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
 | title = Graph Drawing: 13th International Symposium, GD 2005, Limerick, Ireland, September 12-14, 2005, Revised Papers
 | volume = 3843
 | year = 2006| doi-access = free
 | isbn = 978-3-540-31425-7 }}.</ref>

In [[structural rigidity]], the existence of ([[infinitesimal]]) parallel redrawings of a structural framework is dual to the existence of an infinitesimal motion, one that preserves its edge lengths but not their orientations. Thus, a framework has one kind of motion if it has the other kind, but detecting the existence of a parallel redrawing may be easier than detecting the existence of an infinitesimal motion.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Servatius | first = Brigitte | authorlink = Brigitte Servatius
 | journal = Newsletter of the SIAM Activity Group on Discrete Mathematics
 | title = Combinatorics and the rigidity of frameworks
 | url = http://users.wpi.edu/~bservat/siam.pdf
 | year = 1993}}.</ref>
